headline: Mexican Peso Depreciates Past 19 Per Dollar to 17-Month Low on Rate Divergence
summary: The Mexican peso weakened past 19 per US dollar, reaching its lowest level in 17 months as policy rate divergence between Banxico and the Fed narrowed their interest rate differential.
why: Banco de México adjusts domestic monetary policy to balance inflation targeting against international interest rate differentials.

impacts.name: Mexican Peso
impacts.why: The narrowing rate differential between Banxico cuts and Federal Reserve rate policy pressured the peso past 19 per dollar.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Monetary policy divergence between the Federal Reserve and Banxico narrowed yield differentials, weighing on the peso.
